title: Eclipse season, explained
caption: Eclipses need the Sun, the Moon and the lunar nodes in a line, which is why they come in seasons. Save this for the next one.

beats.head: The Moon's orbit is *tilted,* about five degrees.
beats.sub: So most months, it passes above or below the Sun's path.

beats.head: It crosses that path at two points: the *nodes.*
beats.sub: Astrology calls them the North Node and the South Node.

beats.head: Line up the Sun, the Moon and a *node.*
New Moon at a node: a *solar* eclipse.
Full Moon at a node: a *lunar* eclipse.
That lineup comes around about every *six months.*
beats.sub: Each window lasts about a month. That's eclipse season.

beats.head: Astrology reads eclipses as *plot twists.*
beats.sub: Endings, beginnings, and things you can't keep ignoring.

beats.head: In love, that's the *talk* you've been putting off.
beats.sub: Not a reason to panic. A nudge to be honest.

beats.head: Save this for the next *eclipse* season.
